message.content:
Below is a **complete, ready‑to‑run example** that shows how to create a Google Cloud Compute Engine instance that is equipped with an NVIDIA RTX A6000 GPU and runs Ubuntu 20.04 LTS.  
The example uses the **gcloud CLI** (the easiest way to interact with the Compute Engine API) and also shows the equivalent **REST API call** if you prefer to call the API directly.

> ⚠️ **Important note** – As of the latest Google Cloud release, the RTX A6000 GPU is **not** part of the official GPU families that Google offers (Tesla T4, P4, P100, V100, A100, etc.).  
> If you truly need an RTX A6000, you would have to use a custom image or a third‑party marketplace image that contains the driver stack, or you might need to wait until Google adds it to the supported GPU list.  
> For the purpose of this example, we’ll assume you want the **closest available GPU** (e.g., NVIDIA Tesla A100) and show how to specify it.  
> If you do find a custom image that contains the RTX A6000 drivers, you can replace the `image` field with that custom image’s URL.

---

## 1. Using the `gcloud` CLI

```bash
# 1️⃣  Set variables
PROJECT_ID="my-gcp-project"
ZONE="us-central1-a"
INSTANCE_NAME="rtx-a6000-ubuntu"
MACHINE_TYPE="n1-standard-8"          # 8 vCPUs, 30 GB RAM
GPU_TYPE="nvidia-tesla-a100"          # Replace with "nvidia-tesla-a6000" if it becomes available
GPU_COUNT=1
IMAGE_FAMILY="ubuntu-2004-lts"
IMAGE_PROJECT="ubuntu-os-cloud"

# 2️⃣  Create the instance
gcloud compute instances create "$INSTANCE_NAME" \
  --project="$PROJECT_ID" \
  --zone="$ZONE" \
  --machine-type="$MACHINE_TYPE" \
  --image-family="$IMAGE_FAMILY" \
  --image-project="$IMAGE_PROJECT" \
  --accelerator=type="$GPU_TYPE",count="$GPU_COUNT" \
  --maintenance-policy=MIGRATE \
  --scopes=https://www.googleapis.com/auth/cloud-platform \
  --metadata-from-file startup-script=startup.sh   # optional: add a startup script
```

### What each flag does

| Flag | Purpose |
|------|---------|
| `--machine-type` | CPU & RAM allocation |
| `--image-family` & `--image-project` | Ubuntu 20.04 LTS image |
| `--accelerator` | Attach GPU(s) |
| `--maintenance-policy=MIGRATE` | Allows live migration during maintenance |
| `--scopes` | Grants the instance full Cloud Platform access (adjust as needed) |
| `--metadata-from-file startup-script` | Optional: run a script on first boot |

---

## 2. Using the REST API (HTTP)

If you prefer to call the Compute Engine API directly (e.g., from a custom application), you can use the following HTTP POST request.  
Make sure you have a valid OAuth 2.0 access token with the `https://www.googleapis.com/auth/compute` scope.

```http
POST https://compute.googleapis.com/compute/v1/projects/{project}/zones/{zone}/instances
Authorization: Bearer YOUR_ACCESS_TOKEN
Content-Type: application/json

{
  "name": "rtx-a6000-ubuntu",
  "machineType": "projects/{project}/zones/{zone}/machineTypes/n1-standard-8",
  "disks": [
    {
      "boot": true,
      "autoDelete": true,
      "initializeParams": {
        "sourceImage": "projects/ubuntu-os-cloud/global/images/family/ubuntu-2004-lts"
      }
    }
  ],
  "networkInterfaces": [
    {
      "network": "global/networks/default",
      "accessConfigs": [
        {
          "type": "ONE_TO_ONE_NAT",
          "name": "External NAT"
        }
      ]
    }
  ],
  "accelerators": [
    {
      "acceleratorCount": 1,
      "acceleratorType": "projects/{project}/zones/{zone}/acceleratorTypes/nvidia-tesla-a100"
    }
  ],
  "serviceAccounts": [
    {
      "email": "default",
      "scopes": [
        "https://www.googleapis.com/auth/cloud-platform"
      ]
    }
  ],
  "metadata": {
    "items": [
      {
        "key": "startup-script",
        "value": "#!/bin/bash\napt-get update\napt-get install -y cuda"
      }
    ]
  }
}
```

Replace `{project}` and `{zone}` with your actual project ID and zone.  
If you later discover that Google Cloud supports the RTX A6000, simply change the `acceleratorType` to:

```
"acceleratorType": "projects/{project}/zones/{zone}/acceleratorTypes/nvidia-tesla-a6000"
```

---

## 3. Quick sanity check

After the instance is created, you can verify that the GPU is attached:

```bash
gcloud compute instances describe rtx-a6000-ubuntu \
  --project=my-gcp-project \
  --zone=us-central1-a \
  --format="get(accelerators)"
```

You should see something like:

```
[{'acceleratorCount': 1, 'acceleratorType': 'nvidia-tesla-a100'}]
```

---

## 4. Optional: Custom Image with RTX A6000 Drivers

If you need the RTX A6000 drivers specifically, you can:

1. Create a custom image that contains the Ubuntu 20.04 LTS base plus the NVIDIA RTX A6000 driver stack.
2. Use that image in the `--image` or `sourceImage` field instead of the Ubuntu family.

Example:

```bash
gcloud compute images create rtx-a6000-custom-image \
  --source-disk=YOUR_SOURCE_DISK \
  --source-disk-zone=us-central1-a \
  --family=rtx-a6000-ubuntu
```

Then in the `gcloud` command:

```bash
--image=projects/my-gcp-project/global/images/rtx-a6000-custom-image
```

---

### TL;DR

- **gcloud CLI**: `gcloud compute instances create ... --accelerator=type=nvidia-tesla-a100,count=1`
- **REST API**: POST to `/projects/{project}/zones/{zone}/instances` with `accelerators` field set to the GPU type.
- **Note**: RTX A6000 is not currently a supported GPU type on Google Cloud; use the closest available GPU or a custom image if you need that specific hardware.

Happy computing! 🚀
